question.:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 3 \\ 6\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_3=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

For real $x_1,x_2,x_3$, form the equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$. Its augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Carry out these operations in the order shown: $R_2\leftarrow R_2-R_1$; then $R_3\leftarrow R_3-2R_1$; then $R_3\leftarrow R_3-2R_2$. Use the resulting pivots and free variables to decide which statements are true.

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.

:question/answer-fields.:answer-field/key: The equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$ has infinitely many solutions with coefficients not all zero.
The equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$ has only the solution $x_1=x_2=x_3=0$.
